observations: A hooded figure in saturated yellow-orange occupies the center-left against a flat dark green background; the hood casts the face area into near-black shadow.
Within the shadowed face, a small orange square sits above a wide row of white jagged teeth; red crossed lines slash across the eye area, and loose white scribble lines radiate outward from the face.

At the lower left, the sleeve ends in a cluster of dense red and white scratched lines rather than a readable hand; a second cluster of red and white marks appears at the bottom center, both detached from the body's solid yellow mass.
reading: The figure's yellow bulk reads as solid and present, while the face dissolves into shadow broken only by red slashes and bared teeth. That contrast—weight without legibility—gives the image an unsettled feeling. The loose white lines crossing the torso and the frayed sleeve endings resist the idea of a complete body, leaving the figure somewhere between presence and unraveling.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, title neighbor #37 is fully abstract—dense crossing lines, no figure—while #38 anchors that same red, yellow, and dark-green palette to a silhouette. Title neighbor #39 returns to a figure on a dark ground with yellow as the dominant body color.

lookingQuestion: Where exactly does the yellow of the garment end and the background begin along the figure's right side, and what does that edge—or its absence—do to your sense of the figure's boundary?
ambiguities: The lower-left mark cluster could read as a held object or as pure line texture; no clear form resolves it.
nnotb #37 shares the red-yellow-dark-green palette but is fully abstract, making it a color comparison only rather than a structural one; it was not selected as a connection for that reason.
